Reset your Microsoft account password: go to the sign-in page, choose Forgot password, and verify with the phone or email on the account.
Windows Update is stuck: run the Windows Update troubleshooter from Settings, System, Troubleshoot, then restart. If it fails again, run "sfc /scannow" in an administrator Terminal.
Surface will not turn on: hold the power button for 20 seconds, release, then press it once. Charge for at least 30 minutes with the Surface Connect charger.

Article. 8 minutes to read. Applies to Windows 11 and Windows 12.
Windows Terminal is the default console host in Windows 12. It runs PowerShell, Command Prompt, WSL distributions and the Azure Cloud Shell in tabs and panes.
Press the Windows key, type "terminal", and press Enter. Or right-click the Start button and choose Terminal. Terminal (Admin) opens an elevated session.

Each tab runs a profile. Open Settings with Ctrl+, to add one: give it a name, a command line such as "wsl -d Ubuntu" or "pwsh.exe", a starting directory and an icon. Set "Default profile" to the shell you want on launch.

Ctrl+Shift+T opens a new tab. Alt+Shift+D splits the current pane, Alt+Shift+Minus splits horizontally and Alt+Shift+Plus vertically. Alt+Arrow moves focus between panes. Ctrl+Shift+W closes the focused pane.

Set "Launch on startup" to restore your tabs, choose a colour scheme under Appearance, and enable "Acrylic" for a translucent background. Settings live in settings.json, which you can edit directly from the Settings page.

/learn/azure-functions-quickstart.title: Quickstart: your first Azure Function - Microsoft Learn

elements.text: Quickstart: create your first Azure Function in Python
Article. 12 minutes to read. Requires an Azure account, Python 3.12 and the Azure Functions Core Tools.

Run "func init MyFunctionApp --python" then "cd MyFunctionApp" and "func new --name HttpExample --template "HTTP trigger" --authlevel anonymous". This writes a function_app.py with a route decorated @app.route(route="HttpExample").
Run "func start". The tool prints http://localhost:7071/api/HttpExample. Open it with ?name=Azure and you get "Hello, Azure."

Sign in with "az login". Create a resource group, a storage account and the function app: "az functionapp create --consumption-plan-location westus2 --runtime python --runtime-version 3.12 --functions-version 4 --name <APP_NAME> --storage-account <STORAGE_NAME> --resource-group <GROUP>".
Run "func azure functionapp publish <APP_NAME>". The output ends with the invoke URL. Test it in a browser or with curl.
Delete the resource group with "az group delete --name <GROUP>" so the storage account stops billing.

/learn/powershell-scripting.title: PowerShell scripting for beginners - Microsoft Learn

elements.text: Article. 15 minutes to read. Applies to PowerShell 7.5 on Windows, macOS and Linux.
Commands are Verb-Noun pairs: Get-ChildItem lists files, Get-Process lists processes, Set-Location changes directory. Get-Command finds a cmdlet by name; Get-Help shows how to use it.
Cmdlets pass objects, not text. "Get-Process | Where-Object CPU -gt 100 | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 5" gives the five busiest processes as objects you can keep working with.
$name = "report" stores a string; $files = Get-ChildItem *.log stores an array of FileInfo objects. $files.Count and $files[0].Name work as you would expect.

Save this as Rename-Logs.ps1: "Get-ChildItem *.log | ForEach-Object { Rename-Item $_ ($_.BaseName + "-" + (Get-Date -Format yyyyMMdd) + ".log") }". Run it with ".\Rename-Logs.ps1". If scripts are blocked, run "Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser" once.
